instructions.cross_packet_rule: Use cross_packet_terms for likely synonyms, owners, consumers, and seams outside this packet.
instructions.family_key_rule: Every assigned raw family key must have exactly one family_key_assignments row and at least one mapped feature.
instructions.objective: Normalize every assigned validated audit atom into an exhaustive local inventory of distinct Puppet Master features, systems, tools, workflows, GUI surfaces, integrations, data models, governance controls, or cross-cutting concerns. Preserve under-specification, contradictions, unknowns, and explicit non-gaps.
instructions.output_rule: Write exactly one strict-schema JSON payload in the assigned output directory and then return PMR1.
instructions.partition_rule: Every atom_id must appear in exactly one feature.atom_ids array; no omission or duplication.
instructions.research_rule: Do not browse in this phase. Give every normalized feature at least one concrete external-research question for the mandatory next phase; do not treat absence of seed queries as permission to omit research.
instructions.scenario_rule: Give every feature at least one falsifiable scenario requirement for later certification.
instructions.split_merge_rule: Split concepts with distinct lifecycle, authority, consumers, or failure semantics. Merge only true synonyms describing the same product concept; record aliases and relationships instead of collapsing uncertainty.

atoms.statement: The schema identifies a Draft 2020-12 object contract, fixes its identity and title, rejects additional root properties, and requires the complete named top-level evidence surface.
atoms.title: Closed-world root evidence envelope

atoms.statement: The buildability policy encodes a hard non-executable authority boundary: the buildability gate remains false, ordinary product WorkNodes and NodeSeeds remain disallowed, and PNC019 certification remains required.
atoms.title: Buildability remains explicitly disabled

atoms.statement: All eight forbidden artifact categories are required and fixed to zero, including WorkNodes, implementation files, runtime launches, and production build tasks.
atoms.title: Forbidden artifact counts are machine-fixed to zero

atoms.statement: The schema independently validates closed_blocker_families, remaining_blocker_families, and closure_records but declares no disjointness, exhaustiveness, or membership correspondence among them.
atoms.title: Blocker closure collections are not cross-validated

atoms.statement: Payload contract records require ownership, consumer, schema, and negative-fixture strings, but the array has no uniqueness rule and the schema does not resolve or verify the referenced contracts and fixtures.
atoms.title: Event payload registry lacks identity and reference integrity

atoms.statement: Provider-stream lifecycle and recovery obligations are represented only as non-empty strings rather than structured state, transition, error, timing, retry, cancellation, or redaction assertions.
atoms.title: Provider failure and recovery semantics are not machine-checkable

atoms.statement: The GUI wiring section requires command, selector, disabled reason, handler, permission, result, failure projection, and Slint binding fields, but each is only a non-empty string or string list with no relational or state-machine checks.
atoms.title: GUI truth is asserted but not structurally proven

atoms.statement: Preservation-only acceptance is explicitly forbidden and lineage-only terms are explicitly non-behavioral.
atoms.title: Lineage is not accepted as behavioral proof

atoms.statement: Currentness requires a stale-rejection flag plus named CAS, negative-case, refresh-route, and receipt fields, but those obligations are unstructured strings and lists with no cross-field or executable comparison oracle.
atoms.title: Currentness claims lack enforceable CAS semantics

atoms.statement: The shared non_empty_string primitive checks only minLength 1, while string_list checks only array type, minItems 1, and those strings; neither whitespace, uniqueness, format, nor size limits are constrained.
atoms.title: Shared primitives admit low-integrity and unbounded values

atoms.statement: family_list requires at least one member and is used by both closed and remaining blocker collections, making an empty remaining-blocker terminal state structurally impossible.
atoms.title: No-remaining-blockers state cannot be represented

atoms.statement: A closure record fixes its status token and requires evidence, validator, and boundary strings, but the schema neither enforces one record per family nor resolves those references or tests their relationship to the declared blocker family.
atoms.title: Closure records lack uniqueness and evidence resolution

atoms.statement: The shared fixture shape requires given, when, then, negative_case, and owner_refs, but every semantic field is an unconstrained non-empty string and no expected state, error code, side effect, rollback, or oracle structure is defined.
atoms.title: Fixture prose is not a falsifiable behavioral oracle

cross_document_questions: Which canonical contract defines the disjoint and exhaustive relationship among closed blocker families, remaining blocker families, and closure records?

Which validator resolves evidence_refs, validator_refs, payload_contract_ref, schema_ref, negative_fixture, owner_refs, GUI handler locations, and currentness receipts against current canonical artifacts?
Which executable lifecycle contract defines provider ordering, cancellation races, retry idempotency, partial failure, rollback, quota degradation, and terminal-state observability?
Is an empty remaining_blocker_families array a required terminal closure state, and if so which schema owns that representation?

schema designs for executable Given When Then fixtures and negative oracles
provider streaming state machine cancellation retry and partial failure contracts

atoms.statement: This is a Draft 2020-12 object schema with a stable schema identifier, title, and explicit harness-only certification scope.
atoms.title: Receipt identity and bounded purpose are explicit

atoms.statement: The root object is closed and requires identity, status, scope, case, lifecycle, receipt, storage, count, hash, and evidence fields.
atoms.title: Root receipt shape is closed and mandatory

atoms.statement: No schema invariant connects top-level status to case outcomes, storage validations, semantic failures, trace completeness, artifact counts, hashes, or evidence.
atoms.title: Overall status is not derived from certification evidence

atoms.statement: The schema does not require the case_id sets in positive_cases and negative_cases to equal their respective required case ID lists, nor does it require uniqueness.
atoms.title: Declared case coverage is not reconciled with results

atoms.statement: required_lifecycle_steps is not related to lifecycle_trace step_id values, and neither uniqueness nor order is constrained.
atoms.title: Lifecycle trace need not cover the required lifecycle

atoms.statement: event_record_count, validation_count, artifact counts, and the cardinalities of receipt collections are independently constrained but never reconciled.
atoms.title: Receipt counts are not tied to represented evidence

atoms.statement: harness_scoped_artifact_counts permits any nonnegative integer key, including forbidden product-artifact names, and is not constrained by scope_policy.
atoms.title: Harness-scoped counts can contradict the authority boundary

atoms.statement: Negative-case expected_error is not tied to an expected value or code, and emitted_forbidden_artifact_counts has neither minProperties nor required artifact keys.
atoms.title: Negative-case rejection proof is underconstrained

atoms.statement: semantic_failures is optional and constrains only the container type; failure entries, codes, affected steps, remediation, and status coupling are unspecified.
atoms.title: Semantic failure reporting is not a usable recovery contract

atoms.statement: source_hashes requires only one arbitrary key and evidence_refs are only nonempty strings; neither is bound to a required source set, an artifact, a case, or an existence/integrity check.
atoms.title: Hashes and evidence references are not bound to proof subjects

atoms.statement: storage validation_count and validated_family_ids are not reconciled with validations, and validation entries allow arbitrary extra fields.
atoms.title: Storage validation summary can be internally inconsistent

atoms.statement: A lifecycle trace entry requires only step_id and artifact_ref and defines no outcome, transition edge, sequence index, time, retry, failure, or rollback semantics.
atoms.title: Lifecycle trace is not an executable state-transition record

atoms.statement: The pass/fail status vocabulary provides no recovery, rollback, interrupted, superseded, or resumable state semantics.
atoms.title: Failure has no recovery or rollback contract

atoms.statement: Generator ownership and repo-contract use are asserted as constant values rather than proven through executable identity or signed provenance.
atoms.title: Generator authority is asserted rather than verified

atoms.statement: generated_at_utc is the only per-run discriminator, while certification_id is constant and no concurrency or supersession contract exists.
atoms.title: Repeated certification runs lack stable identity

atoms.statement: Artifact payloads are open objects and all reference-like values are generic nonempty strings with no privacy, path, URI, size, retention, or trust constraints.
atoms.title: Artifact and reference data have no trust or privacy lifecycle

atoms.statement: The local_deterministic_clean_room mode is a label with no fields proving network isolation, environment capture, seeded determinism, or clean-room setup.
atoms.title: Local clean-room execution is not evidenced

atoms.statement: The schema provides lower bounds but no maxItems, maxProperties, maxLength, aggregate receipt size, or processing limits.
atoms.title: Receipt size and cardinality are unbounded

atoms.statement: The receipt fixes schema_version to 1.0.0 but this source does not define how producers and consumers migrate or reject later versions.
atoms.title: Schema evolution and migration behavior are unspecified

atoms.statement: The assigned source defines a machine-readable certification receipt, not a GUI surface; accessibility and localization requirements are not applicable within its declared scope.
atoms.title: GUI, accessibility, and localization are out of scope

atoms.statement: Multiple nested evidence structures allow arbitrary additional properties without namespacing, extension ownership, collision behavior, or consumer handling rules.
atoms.title: Open nested objects create undefined extension contracts

atoms.statement: ordinary_product_artifact_counts is a closed six-field object and every artifact count is fixed to zero.
atoms.title: Ordinary product artifact creation is explicitly forbidden

atoms.statement: The schema identifies a harness path but does not identify the publication owner, validator authority, storage owner, callers, consumers, or invalidation authority.
atoms.title: Receipt ownership and consumer boundaries are absent

atoms.statement: CBP-023 correctly denies host authority and forbids silent fallback, but it does not define the normalized blocker outcome fields, state transition, retryability, or receipt linkage for unavailable, blocked, disabled, stale, and degraded host states.
atoms.title: Host capability blockers lack a normalized transition contract

atoms.statement: CBP-001 is unambiguously retained only for migration lineage and is barred from re-owning atomized product coverage.
atoms.title: Retired source-preserving bridge has a clear non-ownership boundary

atoms.statement: CBP-002 declares this document authoritative for product, runtime, storage, UI, and governance details, yet its acceptance criteria only test authority, vocabulary, naming, and references; no concrete UI state or UI acceptance oracle is named.
atoms.title: Facade authority includes UI without a concrete UI oracle

atoms.statement: CBP-003 specifies replayable envelopes, one normalized stream consumer, tool-call reconciliation, auth/UX-state detection, and bounded stream resilience while preserving the orchestration ownership boundary.
atoms.title: Provider facade scope and primary consumers are explicit

atoms.statement: CBP-004 provides a strong negative authority boundary and conditions future actor/account/trust semantics on explicit migration and versioning guidance.
atoms.title: A2A remains external-reference only

atoms.statement: CBP-005 lists the semantic contents of ProviderRequestEnvelope and a typed BRIDGE_INVOKE_OPTIONS projection, but never supplies the canonical envelope's field-level schema, version discriminator, requiredness rules, or serialization oracle.
atoms.title: ProviderRequestEnvelope is canonical in prose but not schema-complete

atoms.statement: CBP-006 defines cwd passthrough but does not define admission-time path canonicalization, binding identity checks, symlink policy, or behavior when the frozen worktree disappears or changes between binding and launch.
atoms.title: Frozen worktree cwd lacks race and staleness guards

atoms.statement: CBP-007 enumerates fields that must survive normalization, but does not define retention duration, overflow behavior, redaction provenance, or atomicity between normalized delivery and storage/retry consumers.
atoms.title: Normalized preservation has no lifecycle or partial-write contract

atoms.statement: CBP-008 requires broad preflight validation and safe redaction, but does not define a rejection event schema, size/depth limits, retryability classification, or whether rejected payload evidence is retained and for how long.
atoms.title: Payload preflight lacks deterministic rejection semantics

atoms.statement: CBP-009 explicitly requires incremental UTF-8/JSONL parsing and structured error events for malformed or incomplete fragments; later CBP-026 supplies concrete buffer ceilings.
atoms.title: Incremental parser behavior is fail-closed and later bounded

atoms.statement: CBP-010 fixes retry counts, timing, jitter, and breaker thresholds, but does not specify idempotency keys, replay deduplication, breaker scope, concurrent half-open probe arbitration, or handling of partial output before reconnect.
atoms.title: Stream resilience constants omit replay and concurrency semantics

atoms.statement: CBP-011 defines explicit unknown fact states and requires resolver acceptance before carrying selected request fields, which closes a major misleading-capability path.
atoms.title: Unobservable capability facts fail closed

atoms.statement: CBP-012 correctly returns no_eligible_adapter instead of unrelated fallback, but 'known recent' 429/5xx evidence has no TTL, account/model scope, reset rule, or conflict resolution with fresh health evidence.
atoms.title: Eligibility filtering leaves recent-failure freshness undefined

atoms.statement: CBP-013 owns switch-reason disclosure and conversational-actor routing but supplies no user-visible presentation, timing, persistence, accessibility, or localization oracle for that disclosure.
atoms.title: Account switch attribution has no GUI disclosure contract

atoms.statement: CBP-014 requires refresh-before-expiry and client reconfigure after credential change but does not define synchronization, in-flight request handling, failed-reconfigure rollback, or cache invalidation completion criteria.
atoms.title: Credential refresh and client reconfigure are not atomic

atoms.statement: CBP-015 gives a concrete no-dispatch outcome for finishReason=length, stable provider-call identity, structured retry classification, and required-schema guards.
atoms.title: Truncated tool calls have a concrete fail-closed oracle

atoms.statement: CBP-016 requires order-boundary disclosure but does not define sequence comparison, duplicate suppression, conflicting replay resolution, or an oracle for repaired ordering.
atoms.title: Ordering disclosure is explicit but repair semantics are not

atoms.statement: CBP-017 clearly retires Gemini CLI account-root behavior and separates Gemini Direct from the active Antigravity CLI lane.
atoms.title: Gemini CLI lineage cannot resurrect an active route

atoms.statement: CBP-018 replaces a stale no-ACP assumption while explicitly preserving transport, account-root, and orchestration boundaries.
atoms.title: Cursor ACP capability is narrowly promoted

atoms.statement: CBP-019 defines a falsifiable route-retirement boundary and prevents aliasing either account roots or provider IDs during Antigravity replacement.
atoms.title: Gemini CLI retirement has a falsifiable absence oracle

atoms.statement: CBP-020 requires version-gated discovery and output-level proof, but does not specify proof expiry, invalidation triggers, supported version ranges, or how route readiness degrades when later probes disagree with stored evidence.
atoms.title: Antigravity runtime proof has no freshness or invalidation rule

atoms.statement: CBP-021 clearly separates Claude print-mode readiness, Cursor print mode, Cursor ACP JSON-RPC stdio, native direct routes, and non-primary opencode-cursor lineage.
atoms.title: Claude and Cursor runtime protocols are not conflated

atoms.statement: CBP-022 explicitly distinguishes CLI installation or lineage evidence from authenticated end-to-end direct-route closure evidence.
atoms.title: Direct-provider closure requires direct-route proof

atoms.statement: CBP-024 names BridgeHandshakeReceipt fields and recovery outcomes but does not define field types, requiredness, protocol negotiation states, binary-hash verification authority, receipt storage, or behavior when terminal restoration itself fails.
atoms.title: Bridge handshake intent lacks a complete receipt and failure schema

atoms.statement: CBP-027 provides a strong fail-closed usage and quota contract with explicit source identity, payload references, unknown states, disabled rendering, and separation of G1 credits from token and cost counters.
atoms.title: Antigravity usage and quota UI truth fails closed

atoms.statement: CBP-026 defines deterministic invocation, bounded streams, normalized exits, and terminate-then-kill behavior, but does not require revalidation that the process group still belongs to the invocation, specify concurrent timeout/cancel arbitration, or define what happens when cleanup receipts cannot be written.
atoms.title: Process-group cleanup lacks identity revalidation and receipt-failure recovery

atoms.statement: CBP-025 is classified gui_related false, yet its canonical constraint directly governs user workflow visibility by forbidding opaque CLI-only state; no consumer or UI oracle shows how that state becomes non-opaque.
atoms.title: Opaque-state prohibition is GUI-relevant despite false classification

cross_document_questions: Which owner defines the versioned ProviderRequestEnvelope schema and projection conformance oracle used by Contracts_V0 and Executor_Protocol?
Do Multi-Account and the GUI owner define accessible, localized, persistent switch-reason disclosure for bridged-provider account changes?
Which runtime contract owns process-group identity revalidation, cleanup-receipt write failure, and concurrent timeout/cancellation arbitration?
Do usage-feature and runtime artifact schemas preserve Antigravity source payload refs and unknown/disabled/credit-only states without coercion?
research_seed_queries: Provider CLI process-group termination PID reuse race mitigation and portable child reaping receipts
Versioned capability handshake downgrade prevention and binary hash attestation for local CLI bridges
Retry replay deduplication patterns for streaming LLM tool-call events with partial output
Accessible account-switch disclosure and quota unknown-state presentation patterns
